request_payload.title: Accumulation of Extracellular GABA, Impaired GABAergic Neurotransmission and 4-Phenylbutyrate Rescue in Mice of SLC6A1 Variant-Mediated Disorders.

mentions.sentence: Mutations in SLC6A1 encoding GABA transporter 1 are a leading monogenic cause of developmental and epileptic encephalopathies, severe neurodevelopmental disorders lacking effective treatments.

candidates.label: 4-Phenylbutyrate / glycerol phenylbutyrate (chemical chaperone)
candidates.summary: An FDA-approved drug (for urea-cycle disorders) that acts as a chemical chaperone, helping unstable or misfolded proteins fold and reach their working location.

candidates.label: 3,4-Diaminopyridine (amifampridine)

candidates.label: scAAV9.P546.SLC6A1 intrathecal gene replacement
candidates.summary: A virus-delivered extra copy of SLC6A1, given into the spinal fluid, to restore GABA re-uptake. First-in-human trial is open by invitation.

candidates.label: Gain of function (the protein does too much)
candidates.summary: The variant protein is overactive: in these disorders that usually means synaptic vesicles fuse too readily, or neurotransmitter is released when it should not

candidates.label: GABA reuptake
candidates.summary: The uptake of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA, 4-aminobutyrate) by neurons or glial cells. This process leads to inactivation and recycling of neurotransmitters.

candidates.label: Loss of function
candidates.summary: The variant protein cannot do its normal job. Used where the evidence shows loss of activity without specifying whether the cause is reduced dose, instability o

candidates.label: Ca2+-triggered neurotransmitter exocytosis
candidates.summary: The release of a neurotransmitter into the synaptic cleft by exocytosis of synaptic vesicles, where the release step is dependent on a rise in cytosolic calcium

candidates.label: Protein destabilization / misfolding
candidates.summary: The variant protein is made but is unstable or misfolds, so it is degraded, aggregates, or is retained inside the cell instead of reaching its working location.

candidates.label: Synaptic vesicle fusion with the active zone membrane
candidates.summary: Fusion of the membrane of a synaptic vesicle with the presynaptic active zone membrane, thereby releasing its cargo neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft.

candidates.label: Dominant-negative effect (the altered protein blocks the good one)

candidates.label: Haploinsufficiency (one working copy is not enough)
candidates.summary: One of the two gene copies is lost or inactive, so the cell makes too little of a protein it needs. The remaining copy cannot cover the shortfall.
